verdict.rationale: Fly.io's own docs say apps can be deployed in regions worldwide so users connect to the nearest server over a global Anycast network. Machines 'run close to your users', and multi-region deployment can be done with a single command. Community reliability complaints concern uptime, not whether regional placement works, so they do not dispute this capability. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the region-selection mechanics (e.g., a region flag or config for choosing specific regions), independent hands-on corroboration of regional deployment.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can deploy my application to specific regions closer to my users

citations.quote: You can deploy apps in regions worldwide, so your users in Tokyo, São Paulo, or Amsterdam connect to the nearest server through our global Anycast network.
Fly Machines are hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second, run close to your users
run an Elixir cluster on multiple servers around the world and deploy to those regions with a single command
